text:
support_julie: FYI — multiple customers reporting p99 spikes (~1200ms) on /v1/generate from APAC clients to eu-west region. Started ~2024-06-27 08:45 UTC, affects ~3 orgs. Logs attached in ticket.
oncall-ryan: ack, digging. Can you paste a sample trace + client region? :eyes:
support_julie: here's a curl and trace header from one customer (s3):
`curl -v -H 'X-Req-Id: c123' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate`
Trace: client=ap-southeast1, route=eu-west, tls_ms=350, dns_ms=40, backend_ms=800
max: do we see backend queuing on model nodes or is this network-only? p95 vs p99 numbers?
support_julie: p95 ~220ms, p99 ~1200ms. Not correlated with increased request rate for those customers. No auth errors.
Also seeing elevated TLS handshake retries in edge logs.
raj-net: sharing quick traceroute from the affected APAC POP -> eu-west: 
```
1  10.1.1.1  1.2 ms
2  192.0.2.5  8.4 ms
3  198.51.100.23  230 ms  <-- long hop
4  203.0.113.2   245 ms
```
raj-net: that 230ms hop looks like a cross-region hairpin; packets bouncing to a transit that adds latency.
alyssa: also seeing spikes in our edge TLS metrics: 0rtt fallbacks + full handshake counts up for those client IPs. Could be DNS geo-miss or anycast path shift.
netbot: sampled routing decisions for c123: POP=ap-southeast1, routed_to=eu-west-1, dns_ttl=30s, last_changed=2024-06-27T08:40:12Z
max: dns_ttl 30s is low. If some authoritative had a mismatch, clients can flip between anycast POPs quickly -> unstable path. Any recent DNS changes or BGP flips?
raj-net: ops pushed a temporary authoritative change to prefer eu-west for some compliance testing at 08:40 — forgot to coordinate with routing. That might explain geo-miss + short TTL.
oncall-ryan: ok — plan: 1) roll back authoritative change, 2) raise TTL to 300s to damp flips, 3) temporarily enable region affinity routing for affected customers. I'll run steps now.
oncall-ryan: rollback applied (cmd: `nsupdate -k /etc/bind/key -v ...`), TTL -> 300s, affinity enabled for orgs custA,custB,custC. Applying in progress :hourglass:
raj-net: watching BGP and edge route tables — I can see paths start to stabilize, traceroute now shows hop 3 ~80ms instead of 230ms for sampled flows.
max: can we add short-term metric alert to notify if tls_full_handshake_rate > baseline + 3sd so we catch regressions earlier?
alyssa: created alert and a dashboard widget for tls handshake retries and route changes. :white_check_mark:
oncall-ryan: status update: 25m after rollback, p99 for affected orgs dropped from ~1200ms -> ~260ms. p95 back to ~180ms. Continued monitoring for 2 hours.
support_julie: passing update to customers — they reported improvement. Thanks team.
max: follow-ups: run a postmortem with action items: (1) DNS change playbook, (2) guardrails for TTL < 60s, (3) change coordination doc. I'll open a small ticket.
raj-net: filing change review. Will add pre-check that flags any authoritative change that would steer APAC traffic to EU with TTL < 120s.
support_julie: closing thread — customers unblocked. :tada:
